text:
Alex L: Heads up — seeing another wave of GPU evictions in eu-west1 this morning. Fragmentation metric spiked to ~62% on gpu-pool-a. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/GPUPOOL/fragmentation
Jordan: Do we know if it's affinity/taint churn or spot preemptions?
Riley: Quick triage: autoscaler shows 3 spot interruptions 08:10-08:25, but most eviction timestamps line up with binpack reshuffles when new long-running training jobs land. PodAntiAffinity is forcing spread across hosts.
Sam: We still have a number of jobs with strict host-level anti-affinity from the legacy training helm charts. That prevents consolidation. Example from a job: 
```yaml
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
```
Alex L: Exactly. Proposed temporary mitigation: change required->preferred for non-critical batch jobs, run a controlled defragmentation (drain/replace) on the worst-fit nodes to consolidate, then evaluate packing. Risk is transient extra evictions during the shuffle.
Jordan: What's the expected cost tradeoff vs risk?
Riley: Current estimate: ~1200 wasted GPU-hours/day in eu-west1 due to stranded GPUs (~62% fragmentation) => approx $6k/day. If compaction reduces fragmentation to ~30% we'd recover ~700 GPU-hours/day.
scheduler-bot: Notice: compaction job scheduled at 1987654345 by Alex L (automated draining will cordon nodes one-by-one).
Sam: Also we should ensure taints for spot pools are respected. Short-lived batch jobs should tolerate them so they can pack into cheaper spot nodes where appropriate.
Alex L: Plan of action:
- Roll config change: required->preferred for podAntiAffinity on batch charts (rolling update)
- Trigger compaction on 5 low-utilization nodes (drain, bounce, let scheduler re-pack)
- Watch evictions and latency for 1 hour, abort if eviction rate > baseline +50%
- Follow-up: convert to a weekly defrag cron and add a rollout verification test
Jordan: Who will own the compaction run?
Riley: I will run it and post commands. Starting now.
Riley: Running sequence: 
kubectl cordon gpu-node-123
kubectl drain gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
(then wait for pods to settle before deleting/recreating the node)
Sam: Reminder: annotate daemonsets and add a rollout annotation so we can track which infra change caused any restarts.
Alex L: Quick update — after compacting 5 nodes fill went from ~38% to ~78% on those hosts. No eviction surge observed in the first 30m.
Jordan: Nice, please capture the before/after charts and open an infra PR for the affinity change.
Riley: Will do. Also proposing we add a weekly low-traffic defrag job (cron) and a dashboard alert for fragmentation >50% sustained over 30m.
Sam: +1 for alerting. Also let's gate the automatic compaction behind a cooldown so it doesn't run during a spot interruption storm.
Alex L: Agreed. I'll draft the PR and the alert rules. Good job all. :thumbsup:
